---

For an index based on a generalized mean of order $\rho$,

$$
\mathfrak{M}_{\rho}(\mathbf{r}, \mathbf{w}) = 
\begin{cases}
\left(\sum_{i = 1}^{n} w_{i} r_i^{\rho}\right)^{1 / \rho} & \text{if } \rho \neq 0 \\
\prod_{i = 1}^{n} r_{i}^{w_{i}} & \text{if } \rho = 0,
\end{cases}
$$
the derivative with respect to $r_{i}$ is
$$
\frac{\partial \mathfrak{M}_{\rho}(\mathbf{r}, \mathbf{w})}{\partial r_{i}} = w_{i} \left(\frac{r_{i}}{\mathfrak{M}_{\rho}(\mathbf{r}, \mathbf{w})}\right)^{\rho - 1}.
$${#eq:euler-1}
Multiplying each of these terms by $r_{i}$ and summing gives the value of $\mathfrak{M}_{\rho}(\mathbf{r}, \mathbf{w})$.

@eq:euler1 is similar to the generalized additive decomposition by @martin2021
$$
 w_{i} \mathfrak{L}_{\rho}(r_i, \mathfrak{M}_{\rho} (\mathbf{r}, \mathbf{w}))^{\rho - 1} \Bigg/ \sum_{j=1}^{n} w_{j} \mathfrak{L}_{\rho}(r_j, \mathfrak{M}_{\rho} (\mathbf{r}, \mathbf{w}))^{\rho - 1},
$${eq:logmean1}
where $\mathfrak{L}$ is the generalized logarithmic mean [@balk2008, Chapter 4]. As with @eq:euler1, multiplying each of these terms by $r_{i}$ and summing returns the values of the generalized mean.

Except when $\rho = 1$ (additive decomposition for an arithmetic mean) or all $r_{i}$ are the same, @eq:euler1 and @eq:logmean1 give different decompositions. This is maybe easiest to see with the additive decomposition of the geometric mean: each $i$ in @eq:euler1 gets the same value.

```{r}
r <- rlnorm(5)

euler_weights <- function(r, weights = NULL, order = 0) {
  weights * (r / piar::gmean(r, weights, order))^(order - 1)
}

euler_weights(r) * r
piar::transmute_weights(r, order = 0) * r
```
